author: Robert Mackey
description:
The Federal Aviation Administration issued a ground stop for all planes due to take off in the US, delaying and canceling thousands of flights

  • Flights grounded at all US airports due to communications outage – live

The US Federal ⁠Aviation Administration said in a statement that the nationwide halt to departures and delays to landings at all US airports that began at about 4pm ET on Friday was caused by “a temporary telecommunications outage”.

“Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis,” the FAA added.

Continue reading...
title: What to know about the rare nationwide ground stop issued by the FAA

author: Abené Clayton
description:
Transportation secretary said stoppage is due to ‘communication issue’ and homeland security says there’s no indication of ‘nefarious attack’

  • Flights grounded at all US airports due to communications outage – live

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a nationwide ground stop for all flights that are due to take off in the US on Friday, delaying or canceling nearly 7,000 US flights, according to aviation tracker FlightAware.

In a post on X, Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, said the stoppage is due to “a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers” and that the FAA’s technicians are looking into the matter.

Continue reading...
title: Nationwide FAA ground stop: nearly 7,000 flights delayed or canceled at airports across the US

author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
description:
Move deals blow to government’s plans to release thousands of prisoners early to tackle prison overcrowding

The government’s plans to release thousands of prisoners early were dealt a blow on Friday after probation officers across England and Wales voted to strike over pay and excessive workloads.

Members of the union, Napo, backed overtime restrictions and other forms of action short of a strike, which is likely to start on 23 November. Plans are being made for strike action to follow at a later stage.

Continue reading...
title: Probation officers in England and Wales vote for strike action over pay and workloads

author: Shrai Popat
description:
New York City mayor says deal will allow bodegas and convenience stores across the country more time to comply

Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor, has struck a deal with Donald Trump to secure a 90-day delay on new rules for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (Snap), so that bodegas and corner stores across the country have time to comply.

The extension, Mamdani said, starts Friday as a result of conversations he had with Trump and Brooke Rollins, the agriculture secretary.

Continue reading...
title: Mamdani and Trump agree to 90-day delay on new food assistance rules for corner stores

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas in New Orleans
description:
Large emergency response underway to rescue people from the water, with overnight cruise ship on its side

  • New Orleans river collision – latest updates

A tanker collided with an overnight cruise ship docked on the Mississippi River in New Orleans on Friday afternoon, prompting an emergency effort to rescue people from the water, according to officials.

The Atlantic Asphalt tanker collided with American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage at about 12.30pm, said Kimberly Curth, the Port of New Orleans press secretary, in a statement. The American Heritage had about 129 passengers – in addition to crew members – onboard when it was hit, according to Curth.

Continue reading...
title: Tanker collides with cruise ship on Mississippi River in New Orleans

author: Chris Stein
description:
Maryland senator’s bid against Chuck Schumer for leadership could decide direction of the Democratic party

  • US politics live – latest updates

Ever since Donald Trump returned to the White House, Democratic officeholders and voters alike have been divided over whether their leader in the Senate, Chuck Schumer, is up to the task of taking the president on.

That debate intensified on Thursday, when the Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen announced he will challenge Schumer for the post of Democratic Senate leader, which will become one of the most powerful jobs in Washington when the party takes control of Congress<
title: As Van Hollen wages a challenge, Senate Democrats are torn on whom to elect as their leader

author: Caroline Davies
description:
Barrister say law does not adequately recognise power imbalance between young people and much older adults

Allegations against Russell Brand and, separately, David Walliams have led to calls for greater legal protection for 16- and 17-year-olds from being sexually exploited by older adults.

A staggered consent law is one route favoured by campaigners, supported by some Labour MPs. Claire Waxman, the victims’ commissioner for England and Wales, has called for “serious conversations” on the potential for legislative change.

Continue reading...
title: Walliams allegations prompt calls for staggered age of consent at 16 and 17

author: Aletha Adu political correspondent
description:
Anneliese Midgley surprises colleagues after Burnham said whips’ office should not be ‘something to be feared’

If Andy Burnham has been accused of being a people pleaser by his critics, the same most certainly cannot be said of his chief whip.

“I’m not going to take any shit and I don’t fuck about,” said Anneliese Midgley, the Labour government’s newest head of party discipline, shedding some light on her direct approach to keeping MPs in line.

Continue reading...
title: Labour chief whip tells Vogue she takes tough approach to keeping MPs in line

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Exclusive: Plans to replace key disability benefits for young people with work and training could affect adults

Downing Street is considering whether plans to replace key disability benefits for the under-25s with work and training should be expanded to older age groups, the Guardian has learned, in a move that risks reigniting Labour tensions over welfare changes.

The prime minister and other cabinet ministers are looking at applying the idea of “participation first” to all working ages, meaning spending billions more on support to enter the workplace while cutting or removing some disability benefits.

Continue reading...
title: No 10 considering expanding under-25s benefits overhaul to older age groups

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
Sales of built units fell to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, with mortgage rates at nearly three-year high

US existing home sales hit a 16-year low in October as buyers were driven away by high mortgage rates and rising inflation, according to new data released on Wednesday.

Sales of already built units dropped to 3.75m in October, down by 8.8% from last year, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) reported. The median existing-home sales price increased slightly to $416,700. Declines in sales were seen in the midwest, south and west, though sales in the north-east held steady.

Continue reading...
title: Home sales hit 16-year low in October amid soaring mortgage rates

author: Gaya Gupta in New York
description:
Local officials warn some services remain unavailable even as Outlook starts to resume normal operations after outage

  • Microsoft outage – live updates

The Microsoft Outlook outage has shaken up companies and local governments across the US that use its suite of email, calendar, video conferencing and cloud storage systems.

Even as Outlook started to resume normal operations Friday morning, local leaders from across the country, including in Miami, Maryland and Los Angeles, warned residents that certain staff or services were still unavailable due to the outage that started around 1pm ET on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Microsoft outage shakes up companies, schools and local governments across US

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
Signing of agreement to smooth movement of food, plants and animals next week will not recoup huge sums firms were forced to spend

The removal of border checks and paperwork on plant imports will “dissolve” £60m of annual costs for the horticulture industry when the UK and EU’s new post-Brexit deal comes in, the environment secretary has said.

Before the UK-EU summit on 20 November, Angela Eagle said she hopes paperwork headaches for importers will “disappear” after the changes, although the move will not help businesses recoup the large sums they spent to deal with border controls.

Continue reading...
title: UK-EU deal will ‘dissolve’ £60m a year of costs for plant trade, says Angela Eagle

author: Jennifer Rankin in Dublin
description:
Kaja Kallas says Moscow is trying to divert attention from its aggression by raising issue of European security

  • Europe live – latest updates

The EU’s foreign policy chief has warned against “walking into the traps that Russia is setting” as she said Moscow was trying to start a debate about European security in order to divert attention from its aggression.

“We have one aggressor and one victim, and the aggressor does not have security concerns,” Kaja Kallas said on arrival at an EU leaders’ summit in Dublin. “Nobody has ever attacked them. They have attacked others. I mean, keep the focus, people.”

Continue reading...
title: Russia is ‘setting traps’ in Ukraine talks, EU foreign policy chief warns

author: Martin Belam
description:
Users of Microsoft Teams and Outlook in businesses and public services reporting problems. Plus would you like to spend time as a helpful furry little post delivery service?

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. A global outage of vital Microsoft systems has crippled businesses and public services around the world. The tech company said it was seeing “early signs of stabilisation” after the failure affected millions of users for more than 12 hours on Thursday and Friday.

Some but not all users were reporting problems with services including Microsoft Teams and Outlook email. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, and more than 90% of Fortune 500 companies use
title: First Thing: Global Microsoft outage chaos as tech firm says there are ‘signs of stabilisation’

author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs correspondent
description:
Parish council of village that declared independence from UK over centre says it will ‘absolutely’ launch legal action

  • UK politics – live updates

Ministers will face a legal challenge over plans to convert a Ministry of Defence site near the Oxfordshire village of Piddington into accommodation for more than 1,200 detained asylum seekers.

It emerged on Thursday that Angela Rayner, the housing and communities secretary, has approved full planning permission, a decision welcomed by the Home Office, who want to end the use of asylum hotels.
title: Planned asylum centre near Oxfordshire village to face legal challenge

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
The 37-year-old was convicted in the state’s supreme court months after a different jury failed to reach a verdict on the same charges

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A former NSW Liberal politician is facing the possibility of a significant jail term after a jury found him guilty of raping a 13-year-old boy.

The former MP Rory Amon was found guilty by a jury, after about four hours of deliberation on Friday, of one count of sexual intercourse with a person aged between 10 and 14 and indecently assaulting a child.

Support for anyone affected by the subject matter of this report is available at Full Stop Australia (1800 385 578).
title: Former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon found guilty of raping 13-year-old boy

author: Ben Quinn and Andrew Gregory
description:
NHS suffering ‘serious’ and widespread disruption, while people are told of possible delays in receiving prescriptions

  • Microsoft outage – live updates

Hospitals, GPs and police forces across the UK have been hit by the global Microsoft outage, as key services battle to get systems back online.

Police forces across the country reported that their systems had been affected, while NHS sources said the healthcare system was experiencing “widespread” and “serious” disruption, with staff reporting being unable to access email and IT systems they use to deliver healthcare.

Continue reading...
title: Microsoft outage hits hospitals, GPs, schools and police across UK

author: Kate Lamb,  Josh Butler and agencies
description:
Few solid clues have emerged as to the true nature of Megaspeed, whose former director Alice Huang has been accused of being a Chinese spy

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

  • From washing dishes at Denny’s to rockstar of AI: the rise and fall of Jensen Huang

A lottery retailer in rural Australia, a dilapidated storefront in Kuala Lumpur, and a near-empty office in Singapore: the global facades of Megaspeed International, the company linked to the downfall of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, form a puzzling corporate picture.

The company, which is registered in Singapore, has registered affiliates acr
title: A baffling trail from Australia to Singapore: what is Megaspeed, the company implicated in downfall of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang?

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Greens retaliate against Labor’s move to run an open ticket in Prahran by leaving the party off how-to-vote cards in 15 seats

The Greens have retaliated against Labor’s decision to run an open ticket in a key inner-city seat by refusing to direct preferences to the party in 15 electorates across the state at this month’s Victorian election.

The move has sparked a war of words between the two parties, with each accusing the other of striking a “dodgy deal” that could help the Liberals and One Nation get elected on 28 November.

Continue reading...
title: Victoria election 2026: Labor and Greens trade accusations of ‘dodgy deals’ as preferences squabble puts key seats on the line

author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
description:
Defence minister says extent of sexual misconduct found by study is ‘unacceptable’, as military tries to attract more recruits

Germany’s defence minister has promised a “zero tolerance” approach to sexual abuse in the armed forces after a study found soldiers, particularly women, faced extensive harassment within the ranks.

The first comprehensive study of its kind into the Bundeswehr, conducted by the Centre for Military History and Social Sciences in Potsdam and released this week, comes as the military is trying to attract new recruits in response to global threats.

Continue reading...
title: More than 60% of Germany’s female soldiers report harassment or abuse

author: Nino Bucci and Jack Larkin
description:
Royal commission also hears from construction company employee who says workers were ‘fearful’ of union

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A major contractor on a troubled Victorian rail project shut down by union officials was warned that the minister’s office felt it would not “have any more work” in the state if it did not resolve the industrial dispute, a royal commission has heard.

The royal commission into the integrity of major public and civil infrastructure construction projects in Victoria heard from a Victorian Infrastructure Delivery Authority (Vida) official for the first time on Friday.
title: Minister’s office said contractor should handle CFMEU or lose work in Victoria, Big Build inquiry hears

author: Jordyn Beazley, Josh Taylor, Adeshola Ore, Achol Arok and Josh Butler
description:
Government services and schools impacted by Outlook and Teams issue as company says fix not ‘taking as expected’

  • Microsoft outage – live updates

  • Microsoft struggles to fix huge outage affecting Outlook and Teams

Australian schools, courts and government services have been hurled back in time to how business used to be done after a global Microsoft outage caused emails and online meetings to go dark.

Australians began reporting issues with Microsoft 365 – which includes Outlook and Teams – just before 5am AEST on Friday, according to Down Detecto
title: ‘Looks like we’ll have to talk to people’: Australia sent back to time before email with major Microsoft outage

author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Danny Vincent and Nathan Law; produced by Guy Szafman and Brian McNamara; executive producers Sami Kent and Alex Atack
description:
Pro-democracy activist Nathan Law and journalist Danny Vincent on the sentencing of the iconic Hong Kong campaigner Joshua Wong to another 10 years in prison. Send your comments and questions to tif.questions@theguardian.com

He has been leading protests since he was 14. Joshua Wong has been on the cover of Time magazine, the focus of a Netflix documentary and an icon for Hong Kong’s pro-democracy movement.

Wong has been leading the fight against a Chinese squeeze on freedoms in Hong Kong for the last 15 years. He will now spend more than 16 years in prison.

Continue reading...
title: Teen prodigy, Netflix star, prisoner: the story of Hong Kong dissident Joshua Wong – podcast

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Exclusive: Former Labor foreign affairs minister says $368bn deal has been reduced to a diplomatic joke

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The former Labor foreign affairs minister Bob Carr says officials in Canberra and Washington acknowledge that the US will never send nuclear submarines to Australia, describing the $368bn Aukus agreement as the two countries “living a lie”.

Carr, a leading critic of the deal, expects American-operated vessels will instead be stationed at bases in Australia, with a future US president likely to determine that China’s military might would make it too difficult for three
title: Aukus deal is ‘living a lie’: Australia will never get nuclear submarines from US and both sides know it, Bob Carr says

author: Jonathan Yerushalmy
description:
Huang’s resignation has sent shockwaves through the AI industry, after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy

  • Full report: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO

  • Analysis: Jensen Huang built an AI kingdom. Now he’s gone, will Nvidia’s ramparts be breached?

Donald Trump has reiterated that it is not yet ‌determined whether Alice Huang ‌was a spy.

In an interview released late on Thursday, the President was asked whether Jensen Huang should have resigned.

The big thing is, was the woman a spy? ‌And I don’t know if that’s been determined yet. But if the woman was a spy, yes. If the woman was not a sp
title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang expected to testify before Congress amid calls for crackdown on China chip exports – live

author: Kat Wong
description:
Former police officer tells court he was attempting to compile statements about ‘bullying from a certain sergeant’ but was worried about speaking publicly

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon has told a Sydney court he obtained a sim card under a pseudonym a month before allegedly murdering two men because he wanted to go to the media about bullying allegations in the police force.

The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and his new partner Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.

Continue readin
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon bought sim card under pseudonym a month before alleged murders, trial hears

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Ann Lawani was taken from her home, sparking a huge outcry among students and faculty at her university

Nearly two months after ICE agents whisked a beloved California nurse and professor from her home in Lodi, her university has ramped up calls for her release.

“She needs to come home,” said Eileen Fry-Bowers, dean for the University of San Francisco’s nursing school,in reference to Ann Lawani, who was arrested by immigration agents in September and has since been shuffled between detention centers in California, Texas, and Louisiana, in a series of opaque transfers.

Continue reading...
title: Calls grow for release of beloved California nurse detained by ICE: ‘We want her home’

author: Dara Kerr
description:
Chief financial officer Colette Kress to take over on interim basis but other names are in mix to be permanent successor

The hunt is on for a new Nvidia CEO. It comes after a whirlwind week, which saw the company head and co-founder, Jensen Huang, resign amid multiple allegations of extramarital affairs, including one that involved an alleged Chinese spy and two with company employees.

Nvidia immediately named Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, as the interim CEO. It’s possible she could stay on permanently, but the company could also name another candidate for the full-time role. Names that have been floated include Ian Buck, who manages Nvidia’s AI hardware and software products, and Rene Haas, a former Nvidia employee and the current CEO of Arm Holdings, a UK-based chipmaker.
title: Who could replace the departed Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO?
